title: Tenant-aware remediation choreography for model-regression incidents
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a tenant-aware remediation choreography and decision matrix for production model-regression incidents that originate during staged rollouts (canaries) across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to standardize triage, automated pause/rollback triggers, customer communication, and fast-path hotfix delivery while accounting for tenant isolation constraints and contractual SLAs.

Scope and intent:
- Cover three deployment modes: Hosted (multi-tenant API), Dedicated (customer-reserved GPU pools), Private/VPC (customer-managed network + audit controls).
- Provide deterministic automated actions (pause canary, redirect traffic, failover to pinned model variant) and manual escalation steps for scenarios where automation is insufficient (encrypted KV cache mismatch, on-prem dependency regressions).
- Include templates and playbook links for oncall, SRE, PM, and support teams.

Key decision matrix (high level):
- Symptom: output-quality regression (BLEU/ROUGE drop or hallucination increase) measured by production evals or customer reports.
  - If regression metric delta >= 15% vs baseline AND customer-visible failures > 0.5% of requests for 5m => pause canary and notify customer success (automated).
  - If latency or OOM regressions cause p50 increase > 2x or 5xxs spike above SLA thresholds => immediate failover to older model variant; create hotfix branch.
- Tenant isolation considerations:
  - Hosted: can pause or rollback globally or by customer API key. Automated routing rules exist to redirect affected keys to previous model variant.
  - Dedicated: cannot change in-customer models without reserved capacity; workflow is to fail open to a compatible, lower-capacity variant or engage capacity manager to provision burst nodes; customer notification required per contract.
  - Private: changes may require customer admin consent or network access; plan for manual rollback windows and customer-appointed liaison.

Automated triggers and tolerances (examples):
- Production test prompts run on canary path every minute. If eval score falls below threshold for 3 consecutive windows (3m), orchestrator emits "pause-canary" event.
- Errors: sustained 5xx rate > 0.2% for 5m triggers "route-to-fallback-variant".
- Resource: per-GPU memory growth > 80% of limit for 2 consecutive minutes triggers allocation probe and canary pause.

Runbook actions (ordered):
1) Initial triage (first 10 minutes): confirm alerts, gather logs (console/model-traces/sampled requests), compute regression delta, tag impacted tenants.
2) Containment (10–30 minutes): if automated rule fires, pause canary and route affected tenants to fallback model variant; for Dedicated, spin up reserve nodes if configured or notify capacity ops.
3) Customer comms (within 30 minutes): use tenant-aware template (see links) to inform impacted customers, include mitigation steps and ETA.
4) Hotfix path (30–120 minutes): create branch from pinned model, reproduce on staging with identical sequence-length distribution and tokenizer; if fixes require model changes, prepare a canary with strict telemetry.
5) Rollout/rollback choreography (post-fix): staged rollout back to affected tenants with decreased concurrency, increased sampling, and auto-abort thresholds.
6) Postmortem and follow-ups: tag root cause, update canary thresholds, add unit/regression test suites and add instrumentation to reduce time-to-detect.

Communication artifacts and links:
- Customer notification templates (PM-approved): https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident-templates/customer-notice-model-regression
- Engineering runbook & playbooks: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/tenant-remediation-choreography
- PR template for hotfix branches: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/.github/pull_request_template.md
- Observability dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/production/model-regressions

Special considerations by deployment mode:
- Hosted: leverage API-key routing to limit blast radius, use pre-provisioned fallback variants. Automation has authority to re-route at route level.
- Dedicated: contractual SLAs require ops coordination; any rollback that affects capacity must be approved by capacity manager and customer success. For severe regressions, coordinate immediate customer-facing rollback only after notifying stake-holders.
- Private: maintain a "customer-liaison" checklist; automated rollback may produce inconsistent states if the customer has on-prem sidecar modifications. Always confirm management-plane connectivity before applying automated changes.

Acceptance criteria / definition of done:
- Clear, tested playbook checked into Confluence and verified by SRE during chaos exercise.
- Automated pause/route/rollback rules implemented in the orchestrator with unit tests and integration tests for three tenancy modes.
- Customer comms templates approved by PM and legal.
- Postmortem template and action items created for any live incident that uses the playbook.

Notes and constraints:
- Avoid global automated model replacement for Private tenants without an explicit customer opt-in.
- Rollback semantics must be idempotent and revert KV-cache migrations if required.

Next steps:
- Finalize thresholds with SRE (actioned in ENG-45124).
- Implement orchestration hooks and policy gates (ENG-45125).
- Schedule a cross-team tabletop exercise with PM, Support, Legal, and two customer engineers.
